source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁבְּת֡וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָ֭אֵלֶּה מֵעֲנ֣וֹת אֶת־אִיּ֑וֹב כִּ֤י ה֖וּא צַדִּ֣יק בְּעֵינָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And ceased the three men the these from answering Job, for he [was] righteous in his eyes.

en.L: And these three men ceased answering Job, because he [was] righteous in his [own] eyes.
en.B: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
en.R: So Job's three friends stopped arguing with him, because Job was sure that he was in the right.

es.L: Y estos tres hombres dejaron de responder a Job, porque él [era] justo a sus [propios] ojos.
es.B: Entonces estos tres hombres dejaron de responder a Job, porque él era justo a sus propios ojos.
es.R: Así que los tres amigos de Job dejaron de discutir con él, porque Job estaba seguro de tener la razón.

fr.L: Et ces trois hommes cessèrent de répondre à Job, parce qu’il [était] juste à ses [propres] yeux.
fr.B: Alors ces trois hommes cessèrent de répondre à Job, parce qu’il était juste à ses propres yeux.
fr.R: Alors les trois amis de Job ont arrêté de discuter avec lui, parce que Job était sûr d’avoir raison.

sw.L: Na watu hawa watatu waliacha kumjibu Ayubu, kwa sababu yeye [alikuwa] mwenye haki machoni pake [mwenyewe].
sw.B: Basi watu hawa watatu waliacha kumjibu Ayubu, kwa sababu alikuwa mwenye haki machoni pake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo rafiki watatu wa Ayubu waliacha kubishana naye, kwa sababu Ayubu alikuwa na hakika kwamba yuko sahihi.

vi.L: Và ba người này thôi không đáp lời Gióp nữa, vì ông [là] công chính trong mắt [chính] mình.
vi.B: Vậy ba người này thôi không đáp lời Gióp nữa, vì ông là người công chính theo mắt mình.
vi.R: Vậy ba người bạn của Gióp thôi không tranh luận với ông nữa, vì Gióp chắc chắn rằng mình đúng.

ko.L: 이 세 사람은 욥에게 대답하기를 그쳤으니, 그가 자기 [스스로의] 눈에 의로웠기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그래서 이 세 사람은 욥에게 대답하기를 그쳤다. 욥이 스스로 보기에 의로웠기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그래서 욥의 세 친구는 더 이상 욥과 논쟁하지 않았다. 욥이 자기가 옳다고 굳게 믿고 있었기 때문이다.

pt.L: E estes três homens deixaram de responder a Jó, porque ele [era] justo aos seus [próprios] olhos.
pt.B: Então estes três homens pararam de responder a Jó, porque ele era justo aos seus próprios olhos.
pt.R: Então os três amigos de Jó pararam de discutir com ele, porque Jó tinha certeza de que estava com a razão.

decisions.choice: these three men: Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar; the debate with them is over
decisions.reason: The three friends came in 2:11 and have spoken in turn since chapter 4. Bildad's last speech was short (chapter 25) and Zophar does not speak a third time, so the debate runs down. Verses 1-5 are prose, the first narrative since chapter 2; they bring in a new speaker, Elihu, before his speeches in poetry begin (32:6b-37:24).

decisions.choice: righteous in his own eyes: he was sure that he was in the right
decisions.reason: "In his own eyes" means in his own judgment (Proverbs 3:7; 26:12). Job had held fast to his innocence to the end (27:5-6; chapter 31), so the friends gave up trying to convince him. The narrator reports how things stood between them; the phrase does not itself say whether Job was right.

decisions.choice: in his eyes, as the Hebrew has it
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek and Syriac translations read "in their eyes": the friends could no longer answer because Job seemed righteous to them. The Hebrew text, followed here, says "in his eyes": Job considered himself righteous.

decisions.choice: Job's three friends; stopped arguing with him; sure that he was in the right (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names the three men as Job's friends and says plainly what "answering" and "righteous in his own eyes" mean here (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced (« cessèrent »), passé composé at Readable (« ont arrêté »)
decisions.reason: The prose of 32:1-6a is narrative, the first since chapter 2. French narrative in this translation uses the written past (passé simple) at Literal and Balanced and the spoken past (passé composé) at Readable; Elihu's speech that follows is in the tenses of speech.

source.text: וַיִּ֤חַר אַ֨ף׀אֱלִיה֣וּא בֶן־בַּרַכְאֵ֣ל הַבּוּזִי֮ מִמִּשְׁפַּ֪חַ֫ת רָ֥ם בְּ֭אִיּוֹב חָרָ֣ה אַפּ֑וֹ עַֽל־צַדְּק֥וֹ נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ מֵאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from [the] clan of Ram; against Job burned his anger, because he justified himself more than God.

en.L: Then the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, burned; against Job his anger burned, because he justified himself rather than God.
en.B: Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, became angry. He was angry with Job because Job made himself out to be in the right rather than God.
en.R: Then Elihu became very angry. He was the son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram. He was angry with Job because Job said that he himself was right and God was wrong.

es.L: Entonces se encendió la ira de Eliú hijo de Baraquel el buzita, de la familia de Ram; contra Job se encendió su ira, porque se justificaba a sí mismo más que a Dios.
es.B: Entonces Eliú hijo de Baraquel el buzita, de la familia de Ram, se enojó. Se enojó con Job, porque Job pretendía tener la razón él, y no Dios.
es.R: Entonces Eliú se enojó mucho. Era hijo de Baraquel el buzita, de la familia de Ram. Estaba enojado con Job porque Job decía que él tenía razón y que Dios estaba equivocado.

fr.L: Alors s’enflamma la colère d’Élihou fils de Barakéel le Bouzite, de la famille de Ram ; contre Job s’enflamma sa colère, parce qu’il se justifiait lui-même plutôt que Dieu.
fr.B: Alors Élihou fils de Barakéel le Bouzite, de la famille de Ram, se mit en colère. Il se mit en colère contre Job, parce que Job se donnait raison à lui-même plutôt qu’à Dieu.
fr.R: Alors Élihou s’est mis très en colère. Il était le fils de Barakéel le Bouzite, de la famille de Ram. Il était en colère contre Job parce que Job disait qu’il avait raison, lui, et que Dieu avait tort.

sw.L: Ndipo hasira ya Elihu mwana wa Barakeli wa ukoo wa Buzi, wa jamaa ya Ramu, iliwaka; hasira yake ikawaka dhidi ya Ayubu, kwa sababu alijihesabia haki kuliko Mungu.
sw.B: Ndipo Elihu mwana wa Barakeli wa ukoo wa Buzi, wa jamaa ya Ramu, alikasirika. Alimkasirikia Ayubu kwa sababu Ayubu alijionyesha kuwa mwenye haki kuliko Mungu.
sw.R: Ndipo Elihu alikasirika sana. Alikuwa mwana wa Barakeli wa ukoo wa Buzi, wa jamaa ya Ramu. Alimkasirikia Ayubu kwa sababu Ayubu alisema kwamba yeye mwenyewe yuko sahihi na Mungu amekosea.

vi.L: Bấy giờ cơn giận của Ê-li-hu con trai Ba-ra-kên người Bu-xơ, thuộc dòng họ Ram, nổi phừng lên; cơn giận của ông nổi phừng lên nghịch cùng Gióp, vì Gióp tự xưng mình công chính hơn Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Ê-li-hu con trai Ba-ra-kên người Bu-xơ, thuộc dòng họ Ram, nổi giận. Ông giận Gióp vì Gióp cho rằng mình đúng chứ không phải Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Bấy giờ Ê-li-hu rất tức giận. Ông là con trai của Ba-ra-kên người Bu-xơ, thuộc dòng họ Ram. Ông giận Gióp vì Gióp nói rằng mình đúng còn Đức Chúa Trời thì sai.

ko.L: 그러자 람 가문의 부스 사람 바라겔의 아들 엘리후의 분노가 타올랐다. 욥을 향해 그의 분노가 타올랐으니, 욥이 하나님보다 자기를 의롭다고 했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러자 람 가문의 부스 사람 바라겔의 아들 엘리후가 화를 냈다. 그가 욥에게 화가 난 것은, 욥이 하나님보다 자기가 옳다고 주장했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러자 엘리후가 몹시 화가 났다. 그는 람 가문의 부스 사람 바라겔의 아들이었다. 그가 욥에게 화가 난 것은, 욥이 자기는 옳고 하나님은 틀렸다고 말했기 때문이다.

pt.L: Então se acendeu a ira de Eliú, filho de Baraquel, o buzita, do clã de Rão; contra Jó se acendeu a sua ira, porque ele justificava a si mesmo mais do que a Deus.
pt.B: Então Eliú, filho de Baraquel, o buzita, da família de Rão, ficou irado. Ficou irado com Jó porque Jó se fazia passar por justo, em vez de Deus.
pt.R: Então Eliú ficou muito irritado. Ele era filho de Baraquel, o buzita, da família de Rão. Eliú ficou irritado com Jó porque Jó dizia que ele mesmo estava certo e que Deus estava errado.

decisions.choice: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram: a new speaker, given a full family line
decisions.reason: Elihu has not been mentioned before and is not named again after chapter 37: he is not among the friends of 2:11 or 42:7-9. His name means "He is my God". Buz was a son of Nahor and brother of Uz (Genesis 22:21), and a people of the desert named with Dedan and Tema (Jeremiah 25:23), so he comes from the same eastern world as Job, whose home is Uz (1:1). The clan of Ram is otherwise unknown. Unlike the friends, he is given a father and a clan, as a young man is introduced.

decisions.choice: his anger burned: he became angry
decisions.reason: Hebrew says that anger, literally the nose, burns or grows hot. The phrase comes four times in verses 2-5: against Job (twice), against the friends (verse 3) and once more in verse 5. The repetition shows the force of feeling behind Elihu's speech.

decisions.choice: justified himself rather than God: claimed to be in the right at God's expense
decisions.reason: The word "from" (min) here compares: Job held himself to be in the right more than God, that is, by insisting he was innocent he made God out to be in the wrong. God puts the same charge to Job in 40:8: "Will you condemn me so that you may be in the right?" The word can also mean "before God" (as 4:17), but Elihu's anger points to the comparison.

decisions.choice: became angry; made himself out to be in the right (Balanced); said that he himself was right and God was wrong (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "became angry" for the burning of anger (m2), name Job where "he" could be unclear, and spell out what "justified himself rather than God" means (m3). Readable splits the long sentence and states the comparison plainly.

decisions.choice: "wa ukoo wa Buzi" for "the Buzite"
decisions.reason: The usual gentilic "Mbuzi" reads as the word for "goat"; "of the line of Buz" names the same people (Buz son of Nahor, Genesis 22:21) without that reading.

decisions.choice: Eliú, filho de Baraquel, o buzita, do clã de Rão (L); da família de Rão (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (as 2:11 announced): the names in their Brazilian forms, "Eliú" as Portuguese has always called him, "Baraquel" and "Rão"; "buzita", from Buz (Genesis 22:21), lowercase as a description like "o temanita". Literal says "clã", the terms doc's word for mishpachah; Balanced and Readable say "família", the everyday word for a family line, as the English Readable says "family". The long line of names is kept whole, since it marks the newcomer (m1).

source.text: וּבִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת רֵעָיו֮ חָרָ֪ה אַ֫פּ֥וֹ עַ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־מָצְא֣וּ מַעֲנֶ֑ה וַ֝יַּרְשִׁ֗יעוּ אֶת־אִיּֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And against [the] three of his companions burned his anger, because that not they had found an answer, and they condemned Job.

en.L: And against his three friends his anger burned, because they had not found an answer, and [yet] had condemned Job.
en.B: He was also angry with his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet they had declared Job guilty.
en.R: He was also angry with Job's three friends. They had not found any answer to what Job said, but they still said that Job was guilty.

es.L: Y contra sus tres amigos se encendió su ira, porque no habían hallado respuesta, y [sin embargo] habían condenado a Job.
es.B: También se enojó con sus tres amigos, porque no habían encontrado respuesta, y aun así habían declarado culpable a Job.
es.R: También se enojó con los tres amigos de Job. No habían encontrado ninguna respuesta a lo que Job decía, pero aun así decían que Job era culpable.

fr.L: Et contre ses trois amis s’enflamma sa colère, parce qu’ils n’avaient pas trouvé de réponse, et [pourtant] avaient condamné Job.
fr.B: Il se mit aussi en colère contre ses trois amis, parce qu’ils n’avaient trouvé aucune réponse, et qu’ils avaient pourtant déclaré Job coupable.
fr.R: Il s’est aussi mis en colère contre les trois amis de Job. Ils n’avaient trouvé aucune réponse à ce que disait Job, mais ils affirmaient quand même que Job était coupable.

sw.L: Na hasira yake iliwaka dhidi ya rafiki zake watatu, kwa sababu hawakuwa wamepata jibu, na [hata hivyo] walikuwa wamemhukumu Ayubu.
sw.B: Aliwakasirikia pia rafiki zake watatu, kwa sababu hawakupata jibu, na hata hivyo walikuwa wamemhukumu Ayubu kuwa na hatia.
sw.R: Aliwakasirikia pia rafiki watatu wa Ayubu. Hawakupata jibu lolote kwa yale aliyosema Ayubu, lakini bado walisema kwamba Ayubu ana hatia.

vi.L: Và cơn giận của ông nổi phừng lên nghịch cùng ba người bạn của Gióp, vì họ đã không tìm được lời đáp, và [thế mà] đã kết án Gióp.
vi.B: Ông cũng giận ba người bạn của Gióp, vì họ không tìm được lời đáp nào, vậy mà vẫn kết tội Gióp.
vi.R: Ông cũng giận ba người bạn của Gióp. Họ không tìm được lời nào để đáp lại những gì Gióp nói, nhưng vẫn cho rằng Gióp có tội.

ko.L: 또 그의 세 친구를 향해서도 그의 분노가 타올랐으니, 그들이 대답을 찾지 못하고도 욥을 정죄했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그는 욥의 세 친구에게도 화를 냈다. 그들이 아무 대답도 찾지 못했으면서도 욥을 죄인으로 몰았기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그는 욥의 세 친구에게도 화가 났다. 그들은 욥의 말에 아무 대답도 하지 못하면서도, 욥이 죄인이라고 말했기 때문이다.

pt.L: E contra os seus três amigos se acendeu a sua ira, porque não tinham achado uma resposta, e [mesmo assim] tinham condenado Jó.
pt.B: Também ficou irado com os seus três amigos, porque eles não tinham achado nenhuma resposta e, mesmo assim, tinham declarado Jó culpado.
pt.R: Eliú também ficou irritado com os três amigos de Jó. Eles não tinham achado nenhuma resposta para o que Jó dizia, mas mesmo assim diziam que Jó era culpado.

decisions.choice: condemned: declared guilty
decisions.reason: The verb (rasha' in the causative) is a law-court word: to declare someone guilty, the opposite of declaring someone in the right (Deuteronomy 25:1; Job 9:20; 10:2). The friends had judged Job a wrongdoer without being able to answer his case.

decisions.choice: and: here "and yet"
decisions.reason: The two clauses stand side by side with a simple "and", but the second is the opposite of what the first would lead one to expect: having no answer, they still condemned him. That is why Elihu is angry with them.

decisions.choice: condemned Job, as the Hebrew text has it
decisions.reason: Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among the "corrections of the scribes", places where the text is said to have been changed out of reverence for God. On that account the verse once read that the friends "condemned God": by failing to answer Job, they made God appear in the wrong. The tradition cannot be checked against any surviving manuscript, and the text as it stands, "Job", makes good sense, so it is followed here.

decisions.choice: any answer to what Job said (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear what the friends could not answer: Job's words.

source.text: וֶֽאֱלִיה֗וּ חִכָּ֣ה אֶת־אִ֭יּוֹב בִּדְבָרִ֑ים כִּ֤י זְֽקֵנִים־הֵ֖מָּה מִמֶּ֣נּוּ לְיָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And Elihu had waited [for] Job with words, for older they [were] than he in days.

en.L: Now Elihu had waited [to speak] to Job with words, because they [were] older than he in days.
en.B: Elihu had waited before speaking to Job, because the others were older than he was.
en.R: Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he was.

es.L: Y Eliú había esperado [para hablar] a Job con palabras, porque ellos [eran] mayores que él en días.
es.B: Eliú había esperado antes de hablarle a Job, porque los otros eran mayores que él.
es.R: Eliú había esperado para hablar con Job porque los otros eran mayores que él.

fr.L: Or Élihou avait attendu [pour parler] à Job avec des paroles, parce qu’ils [étaient] plus âgés que lui en jours.
fr.B: Élihou avait attendu avant de parler à Job, parce que les autres étaient plus âgés que lui.
fr.R: Élihou avait attendu pour parler à Job, parce que les autres étaient plus âgés que lui.

sw.L: Basi Elihu alikuwa amemngoja Ayubu [kusema naye] kwa maneno, kwa sababu wao [walikuwa] wazee kuliko yeye kwa siku.
sw.B: Elihu alikuwa amesubiri kabla ya kusema na Ayubu, kwa sababu wale wengine walikuwa wazee kuliko yeye.
sw.R: Elihu alikuwa amesubiri kusema na Ayubu kwa sababu wale wengine walikuwa wazee kuliko yeye.

vi.L: Vả, Ê-li-hu đã chờ đợi [để nói] với Gióp bằng lời, vì họ lớn tuổi hơn ông về số ngày.
vi.B: Ê-li-hu đã chờ đợi rồi mới nói với Gióp, vì những người kia lớn tuổi hơn ông.
vi.R: Ê-li-hu đã chờ để nói với Gióp vì những người kia lớn tuổi hơn ông.

ko.L: 엘리후는 욥에게 말로 [하기를] 기다렸으니, 그들이 날수로 그보다 나이가 많았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 엘리후는 욥에게 말하기 전에 기다렸다. 다른 사람들이 그보다 나이가 많았기 때문이다.
ko.R: 엘리후는 다른 사람들이 자기보다 나이가 많았기 때문에 욥에게 말하기를 기다렸다.

pt.L: Ora, Eliú tinha esperado [para falar] a Jó com palavras, porque eles [eram] mais velhos do que ele em dias.
pt.B: Eliú tinha esperado antes de falar a Jó, porque os outros eram mais velhos do que ele.
pt.R: Eliú tinha esperado para falar com Jó porque os outros eram mais velhos do que ele.

decisions.choice: had waited with words for Job: held back his own words while the others spoke to Job
alternatives: had waited while Job was speaking
decisions.reason: The verb means to wait patiently (Isaiah 30:18). With "with words" it most likely means that Elihu waited to address Job until the others had finished; it could also mean that he waited through Job's words. Verses 11-12 say he listened to the whole debate.

decisions.choice: older than he: the old speak first
decisions.reason: In the ancient East the aged were expected to speak first and the young to listen (15:10; 29:8). Elihu explains his silence in the same terms in verses 6-7.

decisions.choice: the others (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "They" means the three friends and Job; Balanced and Readable say "the others" so that the pronoun is not taken to mean Job alone.

source.text: וַיַּ֤רְא אֱלִיה֗וּא כִּ֘י אֵ֤ין מַעֲנֶ֗ה בְּ֭פִי שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיִּ֥חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And saw Elihu that there was no answer in [the] mouth of [the] three the men, and burned his anger.

en.L: And Elihu saw that there [was] no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger burned.
en.B: When Elihu saw that the three men had no answer left, he became angry.
en.R: When Elihu saw that the three men had nothing more to say, he became angry.

es.L: Y vio Eliú que no [había] respuesta en la boca de los tres hombres, y se encendió su ira.
es.B: Cuando Eliú vio que los tres hombres ya no tenían respuesta, se enojó.
es.R: Cuando Eliú vio que los tres hombres no tenían nada más que decir, se enojó.

fr.L: Et Élihou vit qu’il n’y [avait] pas de réponse dans la bouche des trois hommes, et sa colère s’enflamma.
fr.B: Quand Élihou vit que les trois hommes n’avaient plus de réponse, il se mit en colère.
fr.R: Quand Élihou a vu que les trois hommes n’avaient plus rien à dire, il s’est mis en colère.

sw.L: Na Elihu akaona ya kwamba hapakuwa na jibu kinywani mwa wale watu watatu, na hasira yake ikawaka.
sw.B: Elihu alipoona kwamba wale watu watatu hawakuwa na jibu tena, alikasirika.
sw.R: Elihu alipoona kwamba wale watu watatu hawakuwa na la kusema tena, alikasirika.

vi.L: Và Ê-li-hu thấy rằng chẳng [có] lời đáp nào trong miệng ba người ấy, thì cơn giận của ông nổi phừng lên.
vi.B: Khi Ê-li-hu thấy ba người kia không còn lời nào để đáp, ông nổi giận.
vi.R: Khi Ê-li-hu thấy ba người kia không còn gì để nói, ông nổi giận.

ko.L: 엘리후는 세 사람의 입에 대답이 없는 것을 보았고, 그의 분노가 타올랐다.
ko.B: 엘리후는 세 사람에게 더 이상 대답이 없는 것을 보고 화가 났다.
ko.R: 엘리후는 세 사람이 더 할 말이 없는 것을 보고 화가 났다.

pt.L: E Eliú viu que não [havia] resposta na boca dos três homens, e se acendeu a sua ira.
pt.B: Quando Eliú viu que os três homens não tinham mais resposta, ficou irado.
pt.R: Quando Eliú viu que os três homens não tinham mais nada a dizer, ficou irritado.

decisions.choice: no answer in their mouth: they had nothing more to say
decisions.reason: The mouth stands for speech. The friends had run out of replies to Job (verse 3). Elihu's anger, already named in verses 2-3, is said once more to explain why he now breaks in.

decisions.choice: became angry (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, Balanced and Readable use the plain English for the Hebrew picture of burning anger.

decisions.choice: "se acendeu a sua ira" (L); "ficou irado" (B); "ficou irritado" (R), the same in verses 2, 3 and 5
decisions.reason: The phrase comes four times in verses 2-5 (m2), so each level keeps one wording for it. Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of burning with "acender-se", which Portuguese also uses of anger; Balanced says "ficou irado", and Readable the everyday "ficou irritado", with "muito" the first time, as the English Readable says "very angry".

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַן׀אֱלִיה֖וּא בֶן־בַּֽרַכְאֵ֥ל הַבּוּזִ֗י וַיֹּ֫אמַ֥ר צָ֘עִ֤יר אֲנִ֣י לְ֭יָמִים וְאַתֶּ֣ם יְשִׁישִׁ֑ים עַל־כֵּ֖ן זָחַ֥לְתִּי וָֽאִירָ֓א׀מֵחַוֺּ֖ת דֵּעִ֣י אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite and said: Young I [am] in days, and you [are] aged; therefore I shrank back and I was afraid from declaring my knowledge [to] you.

en.L: And Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: \q I [am] young in days, and you [are] aged; \q therefore I shrank back and was afraid \q to declare my knowledge to you.
en.B: Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered: \q I am young in years, and you are old; \q so I held back and was afraid \q to tell you what I know.
en.R: Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite said: \q I am young, and you are old. \q So I was shy and afraid \q to tell you what I think.

es.L: Y respondió Eliú hijo de Baraquel el buzita y dijo: \q Yo [soy] joven en días, y {{plural_you:ustedes [son]|vosotros [sois]}} ancianos; \q por eso me retraje y tuve miedo \q de {{plural_you:declararles|declararos}} mi saber.
es.B: Entonces Eliú hijo de Baraquel el buzita respondió: \q Yo soy joven en años, y {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} ancianos; \q por eso me contuve y tuve miedo \q de {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}} lo que sé.
es.R: Entonces Eliú hijo de Baraquel el buzita dijo: \q Yo soy joven, y {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} mayores. \q Por eso me daba vergüenza y tenía miedo \q de {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}} lo que pienso.

fr.L: Et Élihou fils de Barakéel le Bouzite répondit et dit : \q Moi, je [suis] jeune en jours, et vous [êtes] des vieillards ; \q c’est pourquoi j’ai reculé et j’ai craint \q de vous déclarer mon savoir.
fr.B: Alors Élihou fils de Barakéel le Bouzite répondit : \q Je suis jeune en années, et vous êtes âgés ; \q c’est pourquoi je me suis retenu et j’ai craint \q de vous dire ce que je sais.
fr.R: Alors Élihou fils de Barakéel le Bouzite a dit : \q Je suis jeune, et vous êtes vieux. \q Alors j’étais timide et j’avais peur \q de vous dire ce que je pense.

sw.L: Ndipo Elihu mwana wa Barakeli wa ukoo wa Buzi akajibu, akasema: \q Mimi [ni] mdogo kwa siku, nanyi [ni] wazee; \q kwa hiyo nilirudi nyuma, nikaogopa \q kuwatangazia ujuzi wangu.
sw.B: Kisha Elihu mwana wa Barakeli wa ukoo wa Buzi akajibu: \q Mimi ni mdogo kwa umri, nanyi ni wazee; \q kwa hiyo nilijizuia, nikaogopa \q kuwaambia ninachokijua.
sw.R: Kisha Elihu mwana wa Barakeli wa ukoo wa Buzi akasema: \q Mimi ni kijana, nanyi ni wazee. \q Kwa hiyo niliona haya na kuogopa \q kuwaambia ninachofikiri.

vi.L: Ê-li-hu con trai Ba-ra-kên người Bu-xơ đáp lời và nói: \q Tôi [thì] trẻ tuổi, còn các ông [thì] cao niên; \q vì thế tôi đã rụt rè và sợ hãi \q không dám bày tỏ hiểu biết của tôi cho các ông.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Ê-li-hu con trai Ba-ra-kên người Bu-xơ đáp: \q Tôi còn trẻ tuổi, còn các ông đã cao niên; \q nên tôi đã dè dặt và e sợ \q không dám nói cho các ông biết điều tôi hiểu.
vi.R: Ê-li-hu con trai Ba-ra-kên người Bu-xơ nói: \q Tôi còn trẻ, còn các ông đã lớn tuổi. \q Vì thế tôi rụt rè và sợ \q không dám nói với các ông điều tôi nghĩ.

ko.L: 그러자 부스 사람 바라겔의 아들 엘리후가 대답하여 말했다. \q 저는 날수로 어리고 어르신들은 연로하십니다. \q 그래서 저는 움츠러들고 두려워 \q 제 지식을 어르신들께 밝히지 못했습니다.
ko.B: 그러자 부스 사람 바라겔의 아들 엘리후가 대답했다. \q 저는 나이가 어리고 어르신들은 연세가 많으십니다. \q 그래서 저는 물러서서 두려워하며 \q 제가 아는 것을 말씀드리지 못했습니다.
ko.R: 그러자 부스 사람 바라겔의 아들 엘리후가 말했다. \q 저는 젊고 어르신들은 나이가 많으십니다. \q 그래서 저는 수줍고 겁이 나서 \q 제 생각을 말씀드리지 못했습니다.

pt.L: E Eliú, filho de Baraquel, o buzita, respondeu e disse: \q Eu [sou] jovem em dias, e vocês [são] idosos; \q por isso me retraí e tive medo \q de declarar a vocês o meu conhecimento.
pt.B: Então Eliú, filho de Baraquel, o buzita, respondeu: \q Eu sou jovem em anos, e vocês são idosos; \q por isso eu me contive e tive medo \q de dizer a vocês o que eu sei.
pt.R: Então Eliú, filho de Baraquel, o buzita, disse: \q Eu sou jovem, e vocês são velhos. \q Por isso fiquei tímido e com medo \q de dizer a vocês o que eu penso.

decisions.choice: Elihu answered and said: the start of his speeches, which run to 37:24
decisions.reason: The introduction follows the pattern of the other speakers (4:1; 8:1; 11:1). From here Elihu speaks in poetry; the introduction is the verse's first line, as a psalm's title can be. His speeches are introduced at 32:6, 34:1, 35:1 and 36:1, and no one answers him.

decisions.choice: shrank back: was timid, held back in fear
decisions.reason: The verb (zachal) is rare. Its other use describes things that crawl in the dust (Deuteronomy 32:24), so here it pictures the young man drawing back, too timid to come forward.

decisions.choice: my knowledge: what I know, my view
decisions.reason: The word for knowledge here (dea') is used in the Bible only by Elihu (32:6, 10, 17; 36:3; 37:16). It is what he knows and has to say, his view of the matter.

decisions.choice: answered (Balanced); said (Readable)
decisions.reason: Speech introductions in Job follow one pattern: Literal "answered and said", Balanced "answered", Readable "said" (as 4:1).

decisions.choice: shy; what I think (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the young man's timidity and for his "knowledge", which here is his view of the matter (m3).

decisions.choice: plural_you where Elihu speaks to the three friends: "{{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}}", "{{plural_you:decirles|deciros}}"
decisions.reason: Elihu addresses the three older men together (verses 6-14), so the Hebrew "you" is plural; Latin American "ustedes" is the default and Spain's "vosotros" the alternative.

decisions.choice: Elihu calls the three "các ông" and himself "tôi"
decisions.reason: Elihu is the youngest (verse 6) and speaks to his elders with respect; "các ông" with "tôi" is polite without the family warmth of "các bác". He will call Job "ông" as well.

decisions.choice: Elihu speaks to the three in 합쇼체 with "저" and "어르신들" (연로하십니다, 못했습니다)
alternatives: 하오체 with "그대들", as the friends and Job use with each other
decisions.reason: Elihu is the youngest and says so; he speaks up to his elders in 합쇼체, calling them "어르신들". Where he turns aside and describes them or himself (verses 15-22) he uses the plain style, and he will speak to Job in 하오체 (33:1).

decisions.choice: Elihu says "vocês" to the three friends (32:6-16) and "você" to Job (33:1 on)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Elihu's speeches. Elihu is younger and says so, but he argues with the others as an equal (verse 21: he will give no one flattering titles), so he uses the same forms as Job and the friends (JOB_NOTE): "vocês" to the three, "você" to Job. "Os senhores" would add a deference the Hebrew does not have. His more careful style shows in his wording where the English levels show it, not in the form of address.

source.text: אָ֭מַרְתִּי יָמִ֣ים יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ וְרֹ֥ב שָׁ֝נִ֗ים יֹדִ֥יעוּ חָכְמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: I said, days should speak, and abundance of years should make known wisdom.

en.L: I said, Days should speak, \q and [the] abundance of years should make wisdom known.
en.B: I thought, Let age speak, \q and let those with many years teach wisdom.
en.R: I thought, Let the older people speak. \q People who have lived many years should teach wisdom.

es.L: Yo decía: Los días hablen, \q y la abundancia de años dé a conocer la sabiduría.
es.B: Yo pensaba: Que hable la edad, \q y que los de muchos años enseñen sabiduría.
es.R: Yo pensaba: Que hablen los mayores. \q Los que han vivido muchos años deberían enseñar sabiduría.

fr.L: Je disais : Que les jours parlent, \q et que [l’]abondance des années fasse connaître la sagesse.
fr.B: Je pensais : Que l’âge parle, \q et que ceux qui ont beaucoup d’années enseignent la sagesse.
fr.R: Je me disais : Laissons parler les plus âgés. \q Ceux qui ont vécu de nombreuses années devraient enseigner la sagesse.

sw.L: Nilisema, Siku na zinene, \q na wingi wa miaka ujulishe hekima.
sw.B: Nilifikiri, Umri na unene, \q na wenye miaka mingi wafundishe hekima.
sw.R: Nilifikiri, Wazee na waseme kwanza. \q Watu walioishi miaka mingi wanapaswa kufundisha hekima.

vi.L: Tôi đã nói: Ngày tháng nên lên tiếng, \q và năm tháng dồi dào nên bày tỏ sự khôn ngoan.
vi.B: Tôi đã nghĩ: Hãy để tuổi tác lên tiếng, \q hãy để người nhiều năm tháng dạy sự khôn ngoan.
vi.R: Tôi nghĩ: Hãy để những người lớn tuổi nói. \q Người đã sống nhiều năm phải dạy sự khôn ngoan.

ko.L: 저는 말했습니다. 날들이 말해야 하고 \q 많은 햇수가 지혜를 알려야 한다고.
ko.B: 저는 생각했습니다. 나이 든 분들이 말해야 하고 \q 오래 사신 분들이 지혜를 가르쳐야 한다고.
ko.R: 저는 이렇게 생각했습니다. 나이 많은 분들이 먼저 말씀하셔야 한다. \q 오래 사신 분들이 지혜를 가르쳐 주셔야 한다.

pt.L: Eu disse: Os dias falarão, \q e [a] multidão dos anos fará conhecer a sabedoria.
pt.B: Eu pensava: Que a idade fale, \q e que os que têm muitos anos ensinem a sabedoria.
pt.R: Eu pensava: Que os mais velhos falem. \q Quem já viveu muitos anos deve ensinar a sabedoria.

decisions.choice: days, many years: those who are old
decisions.reason: Elihu speaks of age as if it were a person: "days" and "many years" stand for the old men who have lived them. It was a common belief that wisdom comes with age (12:12; 15:10), which Elihu now questions (verses 8-9).

decisions.choice: I said: I said to myself, I thought
decisions.reason: "I said" often means "I thought" in Hebrew (Psalm 30:7; 31:23). Elihu describes what he had been thinking while he waited.

decisions.choice: I thought; age (Balanced); the older people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "I thought" (m2), and turn "days" into "age" or "the older people" (m1).

source.text: אָ֭כֵן רֽוּחַ־הִ֣יא בֶאֱנ֑וֹשׁ וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּבִינֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: But truly, [the] spirit it [is] in a mortal, and [the] breath of [the] Almighty gives them understanding.

en.L: But truly, it [is the] spirit in a mortal, \q and [the] breath of the Almighty [that] gives them understanding.
en.B: But it is the spirit in a person, \q the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding.
en.R: But it is the spirit in people, \q the breath of God All-Powerful, that makes them understand.

es.L: Pero en verdad, [es el] espíritu en el mortal, \q y el aliento del Todopoderoso [lo que] les da entendimiento.
es.B: Pero es el espíritu que hay en la persona, \q el aliento del Todopoderoso, lo que da entendimiento.
es.R: Pero es el espíritu que hay en la gente, \q el aliento del Dios Todopoderoso, lo que les hace entender.

fr.L: Mais en vérité, c’[est l’]esprit dans le mortel, \q et le souffle du Tout-Puissant [qui] leur donne l’intelligence.
fr.B: Mais c’est l’esprit qui est dans l’être humain, \q le souffle du Tout-Puissant, qui donne l’intelligence.
fr.R: Mais c’est l’esprit qui est dans les gens, \q le souffle de Dieu le Tout-Puissant, qui leur fait comprendre.

sw.L: Lakini kwa kweli, [ni] roho iliyo ndani ya mwanadamu, \q na pumzi ya Mwenyezi [ndiyo] inayowapa ufahamu.
sw.B: Lakini ni roho iliyo ndani ya mtu, \q pumzi ya Mwenyezi, ndiyo inayompa ufahamu.
sw.R: Lakini ni roho iliyo ndani ya watu, \q pumzi ya Mungu Mwenyezi, ndiyo inayowafanya waelewe.

vi.L: Nhưng thật ra, [chính là] tâm linh trong người phàm, \q và hơi thở của Đấng Toàn Năng [là điều] ban cho họ sự hiểu biết.
vi.B: Nhưng chính tâm linh ở trong con người, \q là hơi thở của Đấng Toàn Năng, ban cho sự hiểu biết.
vi.R: Nhưng chính tâm linh trong con người, \q là hơi thở của Đức Chúa Trời Toàn Năng, giúp họ hiểu biết.

ko.L: 그러나 참으로 사람 속에 있는 영, \q 곧 전능자의 숨[이] 그들에게 깨달음을 줍니다.
ko.B: 그러나 사람 속에 있는 영, \q 곧 전능자의 숨이 깨달음을 줍니다.
ko.R: 그러나 사람을 깨닫게 하는 것은 \q 사람 속에 있는 영, 곧 전능하신 하나님의 숨입니다.

pt.L: Mas, na verdade, [é o] espírito no mortal, \q e [o] sopro do Todo-Poderoso [que] lhes dá entendimento.
pt.B: Mas é o espírito que há no ser humano, \q o sopro do Todo-Poderoso, que dá entendimento.
pt.R: Mas é o espírito que há nas pessoas, \q o sopro do Deus Todo-Poderoso, que faz com que elas entendam.

decisions.choice: the spirit: the life and mind that God breathes into human beings
alternatives: the Spirit of God in a person
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) means wind, breath or spirit. Here it stands beside "the breath of the Almighty", the breath God breathed into the first human (Genesis 2:7), as in 27:3 and 33:4. Elihu says that understanding comes from this God-given spirit, not from age. It may refer to God's own Spirit at work in a person, as Pharaoh said of Joseph (Genesis 41:38); lowercase "spirit" keeps the line's focus on the spirit as it is in a human being, while the parallel makes clear that it comes from God.

decisions.choice: but truly: a contrast with what Elihu had thought (verse 7)
decisions.reason: The word ('akhen) marks a realization that overturns an earlier view: "but in fact" (Isaiah 53:4; Psalm 31:23). Elihu had expected the old to speak wisely; now he sees that wisdom is God's gift.

decisions.choice: the Almighty: Shaddai
decisions.reason: Shaddai, an ancient name of God, is rendered "the Almighty" (see 5:17).

decisions.choice: a mortal: any human being
decisions.reason: The word ('enosh) means a human being, frail and mortal, men and women alike (as 4:17; 9:2). The pronoun "them" in the second line refers to human beings in general.

decisions.choice: the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The two halves of the verse name one thing from two sides; Balanced and Readable join them into one statement, with the breath of the Almighty in apposition to the spirit.

decisions.choice: God All-Powerful (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "God All-Powerful" for Shaddai in every book.

decisions.choice: "tâm linh" for ruach, "hơi thở" for the breath of the Almighty
decisions.reason: "Thần linh" can be read as a spirit-being, and bare "linh" is unidiomatic; "tâm linh" is the human spirit, as at 21:4, and the parallel "hơi thở" shows it comes from God.

decisions.choice: Readable opens with "사람을 깨닫게 하는 것은" and names the spirit in the second line
alternatives: keep the subject in the first line, as Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: A Korean cleft sentence puts what is explained first and its answer at the end, which is the plain way to stress that understanding comes from God's breath, not from age.

source.text: לֹֽא־רַבִּ֥ים יֶחְכָּ֑מוּ וּ֝זְקֵנִ֗ים יָבִ֥ינוּ מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: Not [the] great are wise, and [the] old understand justice.

en.L: [It is] not the great [in years who] are wise, \q nor the old [who] understand justice.
en.B: It is not the aged who are wise, \q nor the old who understand what is right.
en.R: Being old does not make people wise, \q and age alone does not teach them what is right.

es.L: No [son] los grandes [en años los que] son sabios, \q ni los ancianos [los que] entienden la justicia.
es.B: No son los de muchos años los sabios, \q ni los ancianos los que entienden lo que es justo.
es.R: Ser viejo no hace sabio a nadie, \q y la edad sola no enseña lo que es justo.

fr.L: [Ce ne sont] pas les grands [en années qui] sont sages, \q ni les vieillards [qui] comprennent la justice.
fr.B: Ce ne sont pas les gens âgés qui sont sages, \q ni les vieillards qui comprennent ce qui est juste.
fr.R: Être vieux ne rend pas sage, \q et l’âge seul n’apprend pas ce qui est juste.

sw.L: Si wakuu [wa miaka walio] na hekima, \q wala si wazee [ndio] wanaofahamu haki.
sw.B: Si wenye umri mkubwa walio na hekima, \q wala si wazee wanaofahamu lililo haki.
sw.R: Uzee haumfanyi mtu kuwa na hekima, \q na umri peke yake haumfundishi lililo haki.

vi.L: Không phải những người lớn [tuổi] là khôn ngoan, \q cũng chẳng phải người già [là kẻ] hiểu công lý.
vi.B: Không phải người cao tuổi là khôn ngoan, \q cũng chẳng phải người già hiểu điều gì là công chính.
vi.R: Già không làm cho người ta khôn ngoan, \q và chỉ tuổi tác thì không dạy người ta biết điều phải.

ko.L: 나이 많은 이들이 [다] 지혜로운 것이 아니요, \q 늙은이들이 [다] 공의를 깨닫는 것도 아닙니다.
ko.B: 나이가 많다고 지혜로운 것이 아니고 \q 늙었다고 무엇이 옳은지 깨닫는 것도 아닙니다.
ko.R: 나이가 많다고 지혜로워지는 것은 아닙니다. \q 나이만으로 무엇이 옳은지 알게 되는 것도 아닙니다.

pt.L: Não [são] os grandes [em anos que] são sábios, \q nem os velhos [que] entendem o direito.
pt.B: Não são os idosos que são sábios, \q nem os velhos que entendem o que é justo.
pt.R: Ser velho não torna ninguém sábio, \q e só a idade não ensina o que é justo.

decisions.choice: the great: those great in years, the aged
alternatives: the great, people of high rank
decisions.reason: The word (rabbim) usually means "many", but it can mean "great", and here, beside "the old" in the second line, it most likely means those great in years. Elihu does not say that old people are never wise, but that age alone does not make them so.

decisions.choice: not ... nor: the negative covers both lines
decisions.reason: Hebrew states the "not" once, at the start of the first line, and lets it govern the second line too.

decisions.choice: justice: what is right
decisions.reason: The word (mishpat) means justice, a right judgment. It is the question of the whole debate: whether God treats Job justly (8:3; 34:12; 40:8).

decisions.choice: being old; age alone (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the point as a general statement about age, which is what the two lines mean (m1).

source.text: לָכֵ֣ן אָ֭מַרְתִּי שִׁמְעָה־לִּ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵּעִ֣י אַף־אָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore I say, listen to me; I will declare my knowledge, also I.

en.L: Therefore I say, Listen to me; \q I also will declare my knowledge.
en.B: So I say, Listen to me; \q let me also tell you what I know.
en.R: So I say, Listen to me. \q I will tell you what I think too.

es.L: Por tanto digo: Escúchame; \q también yo declararé mi saber.
es.B: Por eso digo: Escúchame; \q déjame decir también lo que sé.
es.R: Por eso digo: Escúchame. \q Yo también te diré lo que pienso.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi je dis : Écoute-moi ; \q moi aussi, je déclarerai mon savoir.
fr.B: Alors je dis : Écoute-moi ; \q laisse-moi dire, moi aussi, ce que je sais.
fr.R: Alors je dis : Écoute-moi. \q Moi aussi, je vais te dire ce que je pense.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo nasema, Nisikilize; \q mimi nami nitatangaza ujuzi wangu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nasema, Nisikilize; \q niache nami niseme ninachokijua.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nasema, Nisikilize. \q Mimi pia nitakuambia ninachofikiri.

vi.L: Vì vậy tôi nói: Hãy nghe tôi; \q chính tôi cũng sẽ bày tỏ hiểu biết của mình.
vi.B: Vậy tôi nói: Xin hãy nghe tôi; \q để tôi cũng nói ra điều tôi biết.
vi.R: Vậy tôi nói: Xin nghe tôi. \q Tôi cũng sẽ nói ra điều tôi nghĩ.

ko.L: 그러므로 제가 말합니다. 제 말을 들으십시오. \q 저도 제 지식을 밝히겠습니다.
ko.B: 그래서 말씀드립니다. 제 말을 들어 주십시오. \q 저도 제가 아는 것을 말씀드리겠습니다.
ko.R: 그러니 제 말을 들어 주십시오. \q 저도 제 생각을 말씀드리겠습니다.

pt.L: Por isso eu digo: Escute-me; \q também eu declararei o meu conhecimento.
pt.B: Por isso eu digo: Escute-me; \q deixe que eu também diga o que sei.
pt.R: Por isso eu digo: Escute-me. \q Eu também vou dizer o que penso.

decisions.choice: listen: singular
decisions.reason: The command is singular, while Elihu addresses the friends in the plural in verses 6 and 11-14. He may be turning to Job, or speaking to each listener in turn.

decisions.choice: I also: Elihu claims his turn
decisions.reason: "I also" (literally "also I") is emphatic and comes again in verse 17: the young man insists that he too has a right to speak.

decisions.choice: what I know (Balanced); what I think (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, Balanced and Readable put Elihu's "knowledge" in everyday words.

decisions.choice: singular "Escúchame", "te diré"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew command is singular here, though Elihu speaks to the three in the plural around it (meaning decision m1); Spanish keeps the number of the Hebrew, so no plural_you span.

decisions.choice: singular « Écoute-moi »
decisions.reason: The Hebrew command is singular, perhaps turned to Job or to each listener (meaning decision m1); French keeps the number of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "들어 주십시오" with no pronoun
decisions.reason: The singular may be turned to Job or to each listener; Korean keeps Elihu's 합쇼체 and names no hearer, which leaves the question open as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: Escute-me, singular
decisions.reason: The command is singular in the Hebrew (m1), while Elihu speaks to the friends in the plural around it. English "listen" can hide the difference; Portuguese has to choose, and keeps the singular, which may be Elihu turning to Job or to each hearer.

source.text: הֵ֤ן הוֹחַ֨לְתִּי לְֽדִבְרֵיכֶ֗ם אָ֭זִין עַד־תְּב֥וּנֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם עַֽד־תַּחְקְר֥וּן מִלִּֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, I waited for your words, I gave ear to your understandings, while you searched out words.

en.L: Look, I waited for your words; \q I listened to your reasonings, \q while you searched out words.
en.B: Look, I waited while you spoke; \q I listened to your arguments \q while you searched for what to say.
en.R: I waited while you talked. \q I listened to your reasons \q while you were looking for the right words.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, yo esperé {{plural_you:sus palabras|vuestras palabras}}; \q presté oído a {{plural_you:sus razonamientos|vuestros razonamientos}}, \q mientras {{plural_you:buscaban|buscabais}} palabras.
es.B: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, yo esperé mientras {{plural_you:ustedes hablaban|vosotros hablabais}}; \q escuché {{plural_you:sus argumentos|vuestros argumentos}} \q mientras {{plural_you:buscaban|buscabais}} qué decir.
es.R: Yo esperé mientras {{plural_you:ustedes hablaban|vosotros hablabais}}. \q Escuché {{plural_you:sus razones|vuestras razones}} \q mientras {{plural_you:buscaban|buscabais}} las palabras adecuadas.

fr.L: Voici, j’ai attendu vos paroles ; \q j’ai prêté l’oreille à vos raisonnements, \q tandis que vous cherchiez des mots.
fr.B: Voyez, j’ai attendu pendant que vous parliez ; \q j’ai écouté vos arguments \q pendant que vous cherchiez quoi dire.
fr.R: J’ai attendu pendant que vous parliez. \q J’ai écouté vos raisons \q pendant que vous cherchiez les mots justes.

sw.L: Tazama, niliyangoja maneno yenu; \q nilitega sikio kwa hoja zenu, \q mlipokuwa mkitafuta maneno.
sw.B: Tazama, nilingoja mlipokuwa mkisema; \q nilizisikiliza hoja zenu \q mlipokuwa mkitafuta la kusema.
sw.R: Nilingoja mlipokuwa mkiongea. \q Nilisikiliza sababu zenu \q mlipokuwa mkitafuta maneno yanayofaa.

vi.L: Kìa, tôi đã chờ đợi lời các ông; \q tôi đã lắng tai nghe những lý lẽ của các ông, \q trong khi các ông tìm kiếm lời lẽ.
vi.B: Này, tôi đã chờ trong khi các ông nói; \q tôi đã lắng nghe các lý lẽ của các ông \q trong khi các ông tìm điều để nói.
vi.R: Tôi đã chờ trong khi các ông nói. \q Tôi đã nghe các lý lẽ của các ông \q trong khi các ông tìm lời cho đúng.

ko.L: 보십시오, 저는 어르신들의 말씀을 기다렸고 \q 어르신들의 깨달음에 귀를 기울였습니다. \q 어르신들이 할 말을 찾으시는 동안에 말입니다.
ko.B: 보십시오, 저는 어르신들이 말씀하시는 동안 기다렸고 \q 어르신들의 논리에 귀를 기울였습니다. \q 어르신들이 무슨 말을 할지 찾으시는 동안 말입니다.
ko.R: 저는 어르신들이 말씀하시는 동안 기다렸습니다. \q 어르신들의 이유를 귀 기울여 들었습니다. \q 어르신들이 알맞은 말을 찾으시는 동안 말입니다.

pt.L: Vejam, eu esperei as palavras de vocês; \q prestei ouvidos aos seus raciocínios, \q enquanto vocês buscavam palavras.
pt.B: Vejam, eu esperei enquanto vocês falavam; \q escutei os seus argumentos \q enquanto vocês procuravam o que dizer.
pt.R: Eu esperei enquanto vocês falavam. \q Escutei as suas razões \q enquanto vocês procuravam as palavras certas.

decisions.choice: your reasonings: your insights, your arguments
decisions.reason: The word (tevunah) means understanding; in the plural it is the wise arguments the friends put forward. Elihu may use it with some irony, since in his view those arguments failed (verse 12).

decisions.choice: your: plural, the three friends
decisions.reason: Elihu now speaks to the three friends together (verses 11-14), before turning to Job in chapter 33.

decisions.choice: no "Look" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word (hen) draws attention to what follows; Readable leaves it out as a separate word.

source.text: וְעָֽדֵיכֶ֗ם אֶתְבּ֫וֹנָ֥ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵ֣ין לְאִיּ֣וֹב מוֹכִ֑יחַ עוֹנֶ֖ה אֲמָרָ֣יו מִכֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And to you I paid attention, and look, there [was] not for Job [one] refuting, answering his words, of you.

en.L: And I paid close attention to you, \q and look, there was no one refuting Job, \q [no one] of you answering his words.
en.B: I paid close attention to you, \q but not one of you refuted Job \q or answered his words.
en.R: I listened carefully to you. \q But none of you proved Job wrong \q or answered what he said.

es.L: Y a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} presté atención, \q y he aquí, no había quien refutara a Job, \q [nadie] de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que respondiera a sus palabras.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} presté mucha atención, \q pero ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} refutó a Job \q ni respondió a sus palabras.
es.R: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} escuché con atención. \q Pero ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} demostró que Job estaba equivocado \q ni respondió a lo que él dijo.

fr.L: Et je vous ai prêté attention, \q et voici, il n’y avait personne pour réfuter Job, \q [personne] d’entre vous pour répondre à ses paroles.
fr.B: Je vous ai écoutés attentivement, \q mais aucun de vous n’a réfuté Job \q ni répondu à ses paroles.
fr.R: Je vous ai écoutés avec attention. \q Mais aucun de vous n’a prouvé que Job avait tort \q ni répondu à ce qu’il a dit.

sw.L: Naam, niliwasikiliza kwa makini, \q na tazama, hapakuwa na wa kumkanusha Ayubu, \q [hakuna] kati yenu aliyejibu maneno yake.
sw.B: Niliwasikiliza kwa makini, \q lakini hakuna hata mmoja wenu aliyemkanusha Ayubu \q wala kujibu maneno yake.
sw.R: Niliwasikiliza kwa makini. \q Lakini hakuna hata mmoja wenu aliyethibitisha kwamba Ayubu amekosea \q wala kujibu aliyosema.

vi.L: Tôi đã chăm chú nghe các ông, \q và kìa, chẳng có ai bác bẻ Gióp, \q [chẳng ai] trong các ông đáp lại lời ông ấy.
vi.B: Tôi đã chăm chú lắng nghe các ông, \q nhưng không một ai trong các ông bác bẻ được Gióp \q hay đáp lại lời ông ấy.
vi.R: Tôi đã nghe các ông thật kỹ. \q Nhưng không ai trong các ông chứng minh được Gióp sai \q hay trả lời được những gì ông ấy nói.

ko.L: 제가 어르신들께 주의를 기울였는데, \q 보십시오, 욥을 논박하는 이가 없었고 \q 어르신들 가운데 그의 말에 대답하는 이가 [없었습니다].
ko.B: 제가 어르신들의 말씀을 주의 깊게 들었지만 \q 어르신들 가운데 아무도 욥을 논박하거나 \q 그의 말에 대답하지 못하셨습니다.
ko.R: 저는 어르신들의 말씀을 잘 들었습니다. \q 그러나 어르신들 가운데 아무도 욥이 틀렸다는 것을 밝히거나 \q 그의 말에 대답하지 못하셨습니다.

pt.L: E eu prestei muita atenção a vocês, \q e vejam, não houve quem refutasse Jó, \q [ninguém] de vocês que respondesse às palavras dele.
pt.B: Prestei muita atenção a vocês, \q mas nenhum de vocês refutou Jó \q nem respondeu às palavras dele.
pt.R: Escutei vocês com cuidado. \q Mas nenhum de vocês provou que Jó estava errado \q nem respondeu ao que ele disse.

decisions.choice: refuting: proving wrong in argument
decisions.reason: The verb (yakach in the causative) is a word of argument and the law court: to show that someone is in the wrong, to reprove (13:3; 13:10). The friends condemned Job (verse 3) but never proved their case.

decisions.choice: of you: not one of you
decisions.reason: "Of you" stands at the end of the verse for emphasis: none of the three succeeded.

decisions.choice: but (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Look" (hinneh) here introduces what Elihu found, which was the opposite of what he expected; Balanced and Readable say "but".

source.text: פֶּן־תֹּ֣֭אמְרוּ מָצָ֣אנוּ חָכְמָ֑ה אֵ֖ל יִדְּפֶ֣נּוּ לֹא־אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Lest you say, we have found wisdom; God will drive him away, not man.

en.L: So that you do not say, We have found wisdom; \q God will drive him back, not man.
en.B: Do not say, We have found wisdom: \q let God refute him, not a human being.
en.R: Do not say, We have found the wise answer: \q only God can defeat Job, not people.

es.L: Para que no {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: Hemos hallado sabiduría; \q Dios lo derrotará, no el hombre.
es.B: No {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: Hemos hallado la sabiduría: \q que Dios lo refute, no un ser humano.
es.R: No {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: Hemos encontrado la respuesta sabia: \q solo Dios puede vencer a Job, no la gente.

fr.L: Afin que vous ne disiez pas : Nous avons trouvé la sagesse ; \q Dieu le repoussera, non l’homme.
fr.B: Ne dites pas : Nous avons trouvé la sagesse : \q que Dieu le réfute, non un être humain.
fr.R: Ne dites pas : Nous avons trouvé la réponse sage : \q seul Dieu peut vaincre Job, pas les hommes.

sw.L: Msije mkasema, Tumepata hekima; \q Mungu atamrudisha nyuma, si mwanadamu.
sw.B: Msiseme, Tumepata hekima: \q Mungu na amkanushe, si mwanadamu.
sw.R: Msiseme, Tumepata jibu la hekima: \q Mungu peke yake ndiye awezaye kumshinda Ayubu, si watu.

vi.L: Kẻo các ông nói: Chúng tôi đã tìm được sự khôn ngoan; \q Đức Chúa Trời sẽ đánh đuổi ông ấy, chứ không phải loài người.
vi.B: Đừng nói: Chúng tôi đã tìm được sự khôn ngoan: \q hãy để Đức Chúa Trời bác bỏ ông ấy, chứ không phải con người.
vi.R: Các ông đừng nói: Chúng tôi đã tìm ra câu trả lời khôn ngoan: \q chỉ Đức Chúa Trời mới đánh bại được Gióp, chứ con người thì không.

ko.L: 우리가 지혜를 찾았다, \q 사람이 아니라 하나님께서 그를 물리치실 것이다, 하고 말씀하시지 않도록 하십시오.
ko.B: 우리가 지혜를 찾았으니 \q 사람이 아니라 하나님께서 그를 논박하시게 하자, 하고 말씀하지 마십시오.
ko.R: 우리가 지혜로운 답을 찾았다. \q 욥을 이길 수 있는 분은 하나님뿐이고 사람은 못 한다, 하고 말씀하지 마십시오.

pt.L: Para que vocês não digam: Achamos a sabedoria; \q Deus o rechaçará, não o homem.
pt.B: Não digam: Achamos a sabedoria: \q que Deus o refute, não um ser humano.
pt.R: Não digam: Achamos a resposta sábia: \q só Deus pode vencer Jó, e não as pessoas.

decisions.choice: the friends' excuse: the quotation probably runs through the second line
alternatives: Elihu's own reply: God, not a human, will defeat him
decisions.reason: Elihu warns the friends against an excuse for their failure: they have found wisdom, namely that only God can deal with Job. Hebrew has no quotation marks, so the second line could instead be Elihu's own statement. Either way Elihu means to answer Job himself (verse 14).

decisions.choice: drive him back: defeat him, rout him
decisions.reason: The verb (nadaf) means to drive away or scatter, like a leaf or chaff blown by the wind (13:25; Psalm 1:4). Here it means to defeat Job in the argument.

decisions.choice: man: any human being
decisions.reason: The word ('ish) here means a human being as against God, not a man as against a woman.

decisions.choice: Do not say (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "lest you say" warns against saying something; Balanced and Readable put it as a plain command. Literal says "so that you do not say".

decisions.choice: "chúng tôi" in the friends' imagined words
decisions.reason: The three would be speaking of themselves over against Elihu and Job, so the exclusive "chúng tôi" fits.

decisions.choice: the friends' words first, "하고 말씀하지 마십시오" at the end of the second line
alternatives: open with "말씀하지 마십시오" and quote after it
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb of saying after what is said, so "do not say" closes the verse; the quotation stays unmarked, as in the English, and runs through both lines (meaning decision m1).

source.text: וְלֹא־עָרַ֣ךְ אֵלַ֣י מִלִּ֑ין וּ֝בְאִמְרֵיכֶ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And not he has arranged against me words, and with your words not I will answer him.

en.L: And he has not arranged words against me, \q and with your words I will not answer him.
en.B: Job has not directed his words against me, \q and I will not answer him with your arguments.
en.R: Job has not argued with me, \q and I will not use your arguments to answer him.

es.L: Y él no ha dispuesto palabras contra mí, \q y con {{plural_you:sus palabras|vuestras palabras}} no le responderé.
es.B: Job no ha dirigido sus palabras contra mí, \q y yo no le responderé con {{plural_you:sus argumentos|vuestros argumentos}}.
es.R: Job no ha discutido conmigo, \q y no voy a usar {{plural_you:los argumentos de ustedes|vuestros argumentos}} para responderle.

fr.L: Or il n’a pas aligné de paroles contre moi, \q et ce n’est pas avec vos paroles que je lui répondrai.
fr.B: Job n’a pas dirigé ses paroles contre moi, \q et je ne lui répondrai pas avec vos arguments.
fr.R: Job ne s’est pas disputé avec moi, \q et je ne vais pas utiliser vos arguments pour lui répondre.

sw.L: Naye hajapanga maneno dhidi yangu, \q wala kwa maneno yenu sitamjibu.
sw.B: Ayubu hajaelekeza maneno yake dhidi yangu, \q nami sitamjibu kwa hoja zenu.
sw.R: Ayubu hajabishana nami, \q nami sitatumia hoja zenu kumjibu.

vi.L: Và ông ấy chưa bày lời nghịch cùng tôi, \q và tôi sẽ không dùng lời các ông mà đáp lại ông ấy.
vi.B: Gióp chưa nhắm lời lẽ mình vào tôi, \q và tôi sẽ không trả lời ông ấy bằng lý lẽ của các ông.
vi.R: Gióp chưa tranh luận với tôi, \q và tôi sẽ không dùng lý lẽ của các ông để trả lời ông ấy.

ko.L: 그는 저를 향해 말을 늘어놓지 않았으니 \q 저는 어르신들의 말로 그에게 대답하지 않겠습니다.
ko.B: 욥이 저를 향해 말한 것이 아니니 \q 저는 어르신들의 논리로 그에게 대답하지 않겠습니다.
ko.R: 욥은 저와 논쟁한 적이 없습니다. \q 저는 어르신들의 논리를 빌려 그에게 대답하지 않겠습니다.

pt.L: E ele não dirigiu palavras contra mim, \q e com as palavras de vocês eu não lhe responderei.
pt.B: Jó não dirigiu as suas palavras contra mim, \q e eu não vou lhe responder com os argumentos de vocês.
pt.R: Jó não discutiu comigo, \q e eu não vou usar os argumentos de vocês para responder a ele.

decisions.choice: arranged: set out in order, as a case or a battle line
decisions.reason: The verb ('arakh) is used for drawing up an army in order and for laying out a legal case (13:18; 23:4; 33:5). Job's case was set against the friends and against God, not against Elihu.

decisions.choice: with your words: Elihu promises a fresh answer
decisions.reason: Because he has not been part of the quarrel, Elihu claims he can answer Job without repeating the friends' arguments. Readers can judge how far his speeches do so.

decisions.choice: Job (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Job, since "he" follows a verse that ends with God.

source.text: חַ֭תּוּ לֹא־עָ֣נוּ ע֑וֹד הֶעְתִּ֖יקוּ מֵהֶ֣ם מִלִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: They are dismayed, not they answer again; they have moved from them words.

en.L: They are dismayed; they answer no more; \q words have moved away from them.
en.B: They are dismayed and answer no more; \q they have run out of words.
en.R: They are upset and have no more answers. \q They have nothing left to say.

es.L: Están consternados; ya no responden; \q las palabras se les han ido.
es.B: Están consternados y ya no responden; \q se han quedado sin palabras.
es.R: Están desconcertados y no tienen más respuestas. \q No les queda nada que decir.

fr.L: Ils sont consternés ; ils ne répondent plus ; \q les mots les ont quittés.
fr.B: Ils sont consternés et ne répondent plus ; \q ils sont à court de mots.
fr.R: Ils sont troublés et n’ont plus de réponses. \q Ils n’ont plus rien à dire.

sw.L: Wamefadhaika; hawajibu tena; \q maneno yamewaondokea.
sw.B: Wamefadhaika, hawajibu tena; \q wameishiwa na maneno.
sw.R: Wamechanganyikiwa na hawana majibu tena. \q Hawana la kusema.

vi.L: Họ bối rối; họ không đáp nữa; \q lời lẽ đã rời khỏi họ.
vi.B: Họ bối rối, chẳng đáp lại nữa; \q họ đã cạn lời.
vi.R: Họ lúng túng và không còn câu trả lời nào. \q Họ chẳng còn gì để nói.

ko.L: 그들이 놀라서 다시 대답하지 못하니 \q 말이 그들에게서 떠나갔다.
ko.B: 그들은 당황하여 더 이상 대답하지 못한다. \q 할 말이 다 떨어졌다.
ko.R: 그들은 어쩔 줄 몰라 더 이상 대답하지 못한다. \q 더 할 말이 없는 것이다.

pt.L: Estão consternados; não respondem mais; \q as palavras se afastaram deles.
pt.B: Estão consternados e não respondem mais; \q ficaram sem palavras.
pt.R: Eles estão perturbados e não têm mais respostas. \q Não têm mais nada a dizer.

decisions.choice: they: Elihu now speaks about the friends, not to them
decisions.reason: In verses 15-16 the friends are "they", where in verses 11-14 they were "you". Elihu seems to turn aside, to Job or to those listening, and describe the friends' silence.

decisions.choice: words have moved away from them: they have nothing left to say
alternatives: they have removed words from themselves
decisions.reason: The verb ('ataq) means to move on or move away (9:5; 14:18). The words have left them: they are speechless.

decisions.choice: run out of words (Balanced); nothing left to say (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say in plain English what the picture means (m2).

decisions.choice: plain style 해라체 with "나" from verse 15 to 22
alternatives: keep 합쇼체 with "저" as in verses 6-14
decisions.reason: Here Elihu stops addressing the three and speaks about them and about himself (meaning decision m1); descriptive lines inside a speech are in the plain style, with "나", as in the other speeches of Job.

source.text: וְ֭הוֹחַלְתִּי כִּי־לֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ כִּ֥י עָ֝מְד֗וּ לֹא־עָ֥נוּ עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall I wait, because not they speak, because they stand, not they answer again?

en.L: And shall I wait because they do not speak, \q because they stand [there and] answer no more?
en.B: Must I wait because they do not speak, \q because they stand there and answer no more?
en.R: Should I keep waiting just because they are silent, \q standing there with no answer?

es.L: ¿Y he de esperar porque ellos no hablan, \q porque se quedan [ahí y] ya no responden?
es.B: ¿Debo esperar porque no hablan, \q porque se quedan ahí parados y ya no responden?
es.R: ¿Debo seguir esperando solo porque se quedan callados, \q ahí parados sin respuesta?

fr.L: Et attendrais-je parce qu’ils ne parlent pas, \q parce qu’ils se tiennent [là et] ne répondent plus ?
fr.B: Dois-je attendre parce qu’ils ne parlent pas, \q parce qu’ils restent là sans plus répondre ?
fr.R: Dois-je continuer d’attendre simplement parce qu’ils se taisent, \q plantés là sans réponse ?

sw.L: Na je, ningoje kwa sababu hawasemi, \q kwa sababu wanasimama [tu na] hawajibu tena?
sw.B: Je, nisubiri kwa sababu hawasemi, \q kwa sababu wamesimama tu, hawajibu tena?
sw.R: Je, niendelee kusubiri kwa sababu tu wamenyamaza, \q wakiwa wamesimama bila jibu?

vi.L: Và tôi phải chờ đợi vì họ không nói, \q vì họ đứng [đó và] không đáp nữa sao?
vi.B: Tôi phải chờ vì họ không nói, \q vì họ đứng yên mà không đáp nữa sao?
vi.R: Tôi có nên chờ tiếp chỉ vì họ im lặng, \q cứ đứng đó mà không trả lời không?

ko.L: 그들이 말하지 않는다고, \q 그들이 [가만히] 서서 다시 대답하지 않는다고 내가 기다려야 하겠느냐?
ko.B: 그들이 말하지 않고 \q 가만히 서서 더 대답하지 않는다고 내가 기다려야 하겠느냐?
ko.R: 그들이 입을 다물고 \q 대답 없이 서 있기만 한다고 내가 계속 기다려야 하겠느냐?

pt.L: E esperarei eu porque eles não falam, \q porque ficam parados [e] não respondem mais?
pt.B: Tenho de esperar porque eles não falam, \q porque ficam parados e não respondem mais?
pt.R: Será que devo continuar esperando só porque eles estão calados, \q parados ali sem resposta?

decisions.choice: a question: shall I go on waiting?
alternatives: a statement: I have waited, but they do not speak
decisions.reason: The verb form can be read as a statement ("and I waited") or, as here, as a question that expects the answer no. The question fits verse 17, where Elihu decides to speak.

decisions.choice: stand: stand still, stop
decisions.reason: "To stand" here means to stand still and do nothing (Joshua 10:13, of the sun), as people do when they have nothing more to say.

source.text: אַעֲנֶ֣ה אַף־אֲנִ֣י חֶלְקִ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵעִ֣י אַף־אָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: I will answer, also I, my part; I will declare my knowledge, also I.

en.L: I also will answer my part; \q I also will declare my knowledge.
en.B: I too will give my answer; \q I too will tell what I know.
en.R: Now it is my turn to answer. \q I will tell you what I think.

es.L: También yo responderé mi parte; \q también yo declararé mi saber.
es.B: Yo también daré mi respuesta; \q yo también diré lo que sé.
es.R: Ahora me toca a mí responder. \q Diré lo que pienso.

fr.L: Moi aussi, je répondrai pour ma part ; \q moi aussi, je déclarerai mon savoir.
fr.B: Moi aussi, je donnerai ma réponse ; \q moi aussi, je dirai ce que je sais.
fr.R: Maintenant, c’est mon tour de répondre. \q Je vais dire ce que je pense.

sw.L: Mimi nami nitajibu sehemu yangu; \q mimi nami nitatangaza ujuzi wangu.
sw.B: Mimi pia nitatoa jibu langu; \q mimi pia nitasema ninachokijua.
sw.R: Sasa ni zamu yangu kujibu. \q Nitasema ninachofikiri.

vi.L: Tôi cũng sẽ đáp lại phần của tôi; \q tôi cũng sẽ bày tỏ hiểu biết của tôi.
vi.B: Tôi cũng sẽ đưa ra câu trả lời của mình; \q tôi cũng sẽ nói điều tôi biết.
vi.R: Bây giờ đến lượt tôi trả lời. \q Tôi sẽ nói ra điều tôi nghĩ.

ko.L: 나도 내 몫을 대답하겠다. \q 나도 내 지식을 밝히겠다.
ko.B: 나도 내 대답을 하겠다. \q 나도 내가 아는 것을 말하겠다.
ko.R: 이제 내가 대답할 차례다. \q 내 생각을 말하겠다.

pt.L: Também eu responderei a minha parte; \q também eu declararei o meu conhecimento.
pt.B: Também eu vou dar a minha resposta; \q também eu vou dizer o que sei.
pt.R: Agora é a minha vez de responder. \q Vou dizer a vocês o que penso.

decisions.choice: my part: my share of the answer
decisions.reason: The word (cheleq) is a share or portion. Elihu claims his part in the debate, his turn to answer.

decisions.choice: I also ... I also: emphatic repetition
decisions.reason: Elihu says "also I" twice in one verse, as in verse 10: he insists on his right to be heard.

decisions.choice: it is my turn (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my part" means here (m1) and lets the sentence carry the emphasis of "I also".

source.text: כִּ֭י מָלֵ֣תִי מִלִּ֑ים הֱ֝צִיקַ֗תְנִי ר֣וּחַ בִּטְנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For I am full of words; it constrains me, [the] spirit of my belly.

en.L: For I am full of words; \q the spirit of my belly presses me.
en.B: For I am full of words; \q the spirit within me drives me on.
en.R: I am full of words. \q My spirit is pushing me to speak.

es.L: Porque estoy lleno de palabras; \q el espíritu de mi vientre me apremia.
es.B: Porque estoy lleno de palabras; \q el espíritu que hay en mí me impulsa.
es.R: Estoy lleno de palabras. \q Mi espíritu me empuja a hablar.

fr.L: Car je suis plein de paroles ; \q l’esprit de mon ventre me presse.
fr.B: Car je suis plein de paroles ; \q l’esprit qui est en moi me pousse.
fr.R: Je suis plein de mots. \q Mon esprit me pousse à parler.

sw.L: Kwa maana nimejaa maneno; \q roho ya tumbo langu inanisukuma.
sw.B: Kwa maana nimejaa maneno; \q roho iliyo ndani yangu inanisukuma.
sw.R: Nimejaa maneno. \q Roho yangu inanisukuma niseme.

vi.L: Vì tôi đầy dẫy lời lẽ; \q tâm linh trong bụng tôi thúc ép tôi.
vi.B: Vì tôi đầy lời muốn nói; \q tâm linh trong tôi thôi thúc tôi.
vi.R: Tôi có đầy những lời muốn nói. \q Tâm linh tôi giục giã tôi lên tiếng.

ko.L: 내가 말로 가득하니 \q 내 배 속의 영이 나를 몰아댄다.
ko.B: 내 속에 말이 가득하니 \q 내 안의 영이 나를 재촉한다.
ko.R: 내 속에 할 말이 가득하다. \q 내 영이 어서 말하라고 나를 떠민다.

pt.L: Pois estou cheio de palavras; \q o espírito do meu ventre me pressiona.
pt.B: Pois estou cheio de palavras; \q o espírito dentro de mim me impele.
pt.R: Estou cheio de palavras. \q O meu espírito está me empurrando a falar.

decisions.choice: the spirit: the inner breath and urge, given by God
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) means wind, breath or spirit. Here it is the spirit in Elihu that he has said comes from God (verse 8), now pressing to get out, like the wind in the wineskins of verse 19. "Spirit" keeps the link with verse 8.

decisions.choice: belly: the inner self
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the belly is the seat of thought and feeling, the innermost part of a person (15:35; Proverbs 18:8; 20:27). It returns in verse 19.

decisions.choice: presses me: constrains, urges me on
decisions.reason: The verb (tsuq) means to press hard or put under pressure (Judges 14:17; 16:16).

decisions.choice: within me (Balanced); my spirit (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Belly" as the inner self is not natural English (m2); Balanced says "within me", Readable "my spirit". Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: הִנֵּֽה־בִטְנִ֗י כְּיַ֥יִן לֹא־יִפָּתֵ֑חַ כְּאֹב֥וֹת חֲ֝דָשִׁ֗ים יִבָּקֵֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, my belly [is] like wine not opened; like new wineskins it will burst.

en.L: Look, my belly [is] like wine [that] is not opened; \q like new wineskins it is about to burst.
en.B: Look, inside I am like wine with no vent; \q like new wineskins, I am ready to burst.
en.R: Inside, I am like wine sealed up with no way for the air to escape. \q Like new wineskins, I am ready to burst.

es.L: He aquí, mi vientre [es] como vino [que] no se ha destapado; \q como odres nuevos está a punto de reventar.
es.B: Por dentro soy como vino sin respiradero; \q como odres nuevos, estoy a punto de reventar.
es.R: Por dentro soy como vino encerrado, sin salida para el aire. \q Como odres nuevos, estoy a punto de reventar.

fr.L: Voici, mon ventre [est] comme un vin [qui] n’est pas ouvert ; \q comme des outres neuves, il va éclater.
fr.B: Voici, au-dedans je suis comme un vin sans issue ; \q comme des outres neuves, je suis près d’éclater.
fr.R: Au-dedans, je suis comme du vin enfermé, sans moyen pour l’air de sortir. \q Comme des outres neuves, je suis prêt à éclater.

sw.L: Tazama, tumbo langu [ni] kama divai isiyofunguliwa; \q kama viriba vipya liko karibu kupasuka.
sw.B: Tazama, ndani yangu niko kama divai isiyo na pa kutokea; \q kama viriba vipya, niko tayari kupasuka.
sw.R: Ndani yangu niko kama divai iliyofungwa bila njia ya hewa kutoka. \q Kama viriba vipya, niko tayari kupasuka.

vi.L: Kìa, bụng tôi [như] rượu chưa được mở ra; \q như bầu da mới, nó sắp nứt vỡ.
vi.B: Kìa, lòng tôi như rượu không có lỗ thoát hơi; \q như bầu da mới, tôi sắp vỡ tung.
vi.R: Trong lòng tôi như rượu bị nút kín, hơi không thoát ra được. \q Như bầu da mới, tôi sắp vỡ tung.

ko.L: 보라, 내 배는 열리지 않은 포도주 같아서 \q 새 가죽 부대처럼 터지려 한다.
ko.B: 보라, 내 속은 숨구멍 없는 포도주 같아서 \q 새 가죽 부대처럼 터질 것만 같다.
ko.R: 내 속은 공기가 빠져나갈 틈 없이 막아 둔 포도주 같다. \q 새 가죽 부대처럼 곧 터질 것 같다.

pt.L: Veja, o meu ventre [é] como vinho [que] não foi aberto; \q como odres novos está para rebentar.
pt.B: Veja, por dentro eu sou como vinho sem respiro; \q como odres novos, estou para rebentar.
pt.R: Por dentro eu sou como vinho fechado, sem ter por onde o ar sair. \q Como odres novos, estou para estourar.

decisions.choice: wine not opened, wineskins about to burst: fermenting wine in a sealed skin
decisions.reason: Wine was stored in skins. As new wine ferments, its gas swells the skin, and if it has no vent the skin splits (Matthew 9:17). Elihu's words, held back for so long, press to come out in the same way.

decisions.choice: new wineskins: perhaps "skins of new wine"
decisions.reason: New skins stretch more easily than old ones, so it is surprising that they should burst. The phrase may mean skins holding new wine, still fermenting; the image is the same either way: a container about to give way.

decisions.choice: inside I am (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18, Balanced and Readable say "inside" for the belly as the inner self.

source.text: אֲדַבְּרָ֥ה וְיִֽרְוַֽח־לִ֑י אֶפְתַּ֖ח שְׂפָתַ֣י וְאֶֽעֱנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Let me speak, and it may be relief to me; let me open my lips and answer.

en.L: Let me speak, so that it may be relief to me; \q let me open my lips and answer.
en.B: I must speak and find relief; \q I must open my lips and answer.
en.R: I must speak so that I can feel better. \q I must open my mouth and answer.

es.L: Que yo hable, para hallar alivio; \q que abra mis labios y responda.
es.B: Tengo que hablar y hallar alivio; \q tengo que abrir mis labios y responder.
es.R: Tengo que hablar para sentirme mejor. \q Tengo que abrir la boca y responder.

fr.L: Que je parle, pour que j’aie du soulagement ; \q que j’ouvre mes lèvres et que je réponde.
fr.B: Il me faut parler pour être soulagé ; \q il me faut ouvrir les lèvres et répondre.
fr.R: Je dois parler pour me sentir mieux. \q Je dois ouvrir la bouche et répondre.

sw.L: Na niseme, ili nipate nafuu; \q na nifumbue midomo yangu nijibu.
sw.B: Lazima niseme nipate nafuu; \q lazima nifumbue midomo yangu nijibu.
sw.R: Lazima niseme ili nijisikie vizuri. \q Lazima nifungue kinywa changu nijibu.

vi.L: Hãy để tôi nói, để tôi được nhẹ nhõm; \q hãy để tôi mở môi và đáp lời.
vi.B: Tôi phải nói ra cho được nhẹ lòng; \q tôi phải mở môi mà đáp lời.
vi.R: Tôi phải nói ra để thấy dễ chịu hơn. \q Tôi phải mở miệng mà trả lời.

ko.L: 내가 말하련다, 그러면 내게 숨통이 트일 것이다. \q 내 입술을 열고 대답하련다.
ko.B: 나는 말해야 숨통이 트이겠다. \q 입술을 열고 대답해야겠다.
ko.R: 말을 해야 속이 시원해지겠다. \q 입을 열고 대답해야겠다.

pt.L: Deixe-me falar, para que haja alívio para mim; \q deixe-me abrir os meus lábios e responder.
pt.B: Tenho de falar e encontrar alívio; \q tenho de abrir os lábios e responder.
pt.R: Tenho de falar para me sentir melhor. \q Tenho de abrir a boca e responder.

decisions.choice: relief: room to breathe
decisions.reason: The verb (ravach) means to be spacious, to have room, and so to find relief (1 Samuel 16:23). It sounds like the word for spirit or wind (ruach) in verse 18: once the pent-up wind is let out, Elihu can breathe again.

decisions.choice: I must (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verbs express Elihu's resolve; "I must" carries their urgency after verses 18-19.

source.text: אַל־נָ֭א אֶשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְאֶל־אָ֝דָ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲכַנֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Not please let me lift up [the] face of anyone, and to a human not I will give flattering titles.

en.L: Let me not lift up the face of anyone, \q and to any human I will not give flattering titles.
en.B: I will not take anyone's side, \q nor flatter any human being.
en.R: I will not favor anyone, \q and I will not use fancy titles to flatter anyone.

es.L: Que no levante yo el rostro de nadie, \q ni a ningún ser humano le dé títulos lisonjeros.
es.B: No me pondré de parte de nadie, \q ni adularé a ningún ser humano.
es.R: No favoreceré a nadie, \q y no usaré títulos bonitos para halagar a nadie.

fr.L: Que je ne relève pas la face de qui que ce soit, \q et à aucun humain je ne donnerai de titres flatteurs.
fr.B: Je ne prendrai le parti de personne, \q et je ne flatterai aucun être humain.
fr.R: Je ne favoriserai personne, \q et je n’utiliserai pas de beaux titres pour flatter qui que ce soit.

sw.L: Nisiuinue uso wa mtu yeyote, \q wala sitampa mwanadamu yeyote majina ya kujipendekeza.
sw.B: Sitampendelea mtu yeyote, \q wala sitambembeleza mwanadamu yeyote.
sw.R: Sitampendelea mtu yeyote, \q wala sitatumia vyeo vya kupendeza ili kumbembeleza mtu.

vi.L: Xin cho tôi đừng nể mặt bất cứ ai, \q và tôi sẽ không dùng danh hiệu tâng bốc với bất cứ người nào.
vi.B: Tôi sẽ không đứng về phe ai, \q cũng chẳng nịnh hót người nào.
vi.R: Tôi sẽ không thiên vị ai, \q và sẽ không dùng những danh xưng hoa mỹ để nịnh bợ ai.

ko.L: 나는 누구의 얼굴도 들어 주지 않겠고 \q 어떤 사람에게도 아첨하는 칭호를 붙이지 않겠다.
ko.B: 나는 누구의 편도 들지 않고 \q 어떤 사람에게도 아첨하지 않겠다.
ko.R: 나는 누구도 봐주지 않겠다. \q 듣기 좋은 호칭으로 누구에게 아첨하지도 않겠다.

pt.L: Que eu não levante o rosto de ninguém, \q e a nenhum ser humano darei títulos lisonjeiros.
pt.B: Não vou tomar o partido de ninguém, \q nem bajular nenhum ser humano.
pt.R: Não vou favorecer ninguém \q nem usar títulos bonitos para bajular as pessoas.

decisions.choice: lift up the face of: show favor, take sides
decisions.reason: To "lift someone's face" is to accept or favor them, and in a dispute to be partial (Leviticus 19:15; Job 13:8, 10). Elihu promises to judge the case fairly, without deference to the older men or to Job.

decisions.choice: give flattering titles: address with honorific names
decisions.reason: The verb (kanah) means to give someone a title or a name of honor (Isaiah 44:5; 45:4). Elihu will not use the polite flattery that a young man might owe his elders.

decisions.choice: take anyone's side (Balanced); favor (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1); Literal keeps the picture.

records.literal_gloss: For not I know [how] to give flattering titles; in a little would carry me away my Maker.

en.L: For I do not know [how] to flatter; \q [else] in a little [while] my Maker would carry me away.
en.B: For I do not know how to flatter; \q if I did, my Maker would soon carry me away.
en.R: I do not know how to flatter people. \q If I did, God who made me would soon put an end to me.

es.L: Porque no sé [cómo] lisonjear; \q [si no], en poco [tiempo] me llevaría mi Hacedor.
es.B: Porque no sé adular; \q si lo hiciera, mi Hacedor pronto me llevaría.
es.R: No sé halagar a la gente. \q Si lo hiciera, Dios, que me creó, pronto acabaría conmigo.

fr.L: Car je ne sais pas flatter ; \q [sinon], en peu [de temps] mon Créateur m’emporterait.
fr.B: Car je ne sais pas flatter ; \q si je le faisais, mon Créateur m’emporterait bientôt.
fr.R: Je ne sais pas flatter les gens. \q Si je le faisais, Dieu, qui m’a créé, en finirait vite avec moi.

sw.L: Kwa maana sijui [jinsi ya] kujipendekeza; \q [la sivyo] kwa muda [mfupi] Muumba wangu angeniondoa.
sw.B: Kwa maana sijui kubembeleza; \q kama ningefanya hivyo, Muumba wangu angeniondoa upesi.
sw.R: Sijui kuwabembeleza watu. \q Kama ningefanya hivyo, Mungu aliyeniumba angenimaliza upesi.

vi.L: Vì tôi không biết [cách] nịnh hót; \q [nếu không], trong chốc lát Đấng Tạo Hóa của tôi sẽ cất tôi đi.
vi.B: Vì tôi không biết nịnh hót; \q nếu tôi làm thế, Đấng Tạo Hóa của tôi sẽ sớm cất tôi đi.
vi.R: Tôi không biết nịnh bợ người ta. \q Nếu tôi làm thế, Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng dựng nên tôi, sẽ sớm dứt bỏ tôi.

ko.L: 나는 아첨할 줄 모른다. \q [그렇지 않으면] 나를 지으신 분이 곧 나를 데려가실 것이다.
ko.B: 나는 아첨할 줄 모른다. \q 만일 아첨한다면 나를 지으신 분이 곧 나를 없애 버리실 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 사람들에게 아첨할 줄 모른다. \q 만일 그런다면 나를 지으신 하나님께서 곧 나를 끝장내실 것이다.

pt.L: Pois não sei lisonjear; \q [senão,] em pouco [tempo] o meu Criador me levaria embora.
pt.B: Pois não sei bajular; \q se soubesse, o meu Criador logo me levaria embora.
pt.R: Eu não sei bajular as pessoas. \q Se fizesse isso, Deus, que me criou, logo acabaria comigo.

decisions.choice: [else]: an unstated condition
decisions.reason: The second line leaves its condition unspoken: if Elihu were to flatter, God would soon remove him. Hebrew often lets the context supply such an "if".

decisions.choice: carry me away: remove, sweep away in judgment
decisions.reason: The verb (nasa') means to lift and carry off; used of the wind carrying away the wicked (27:21), it means sudden death or ruin.

decisions.choice: my Maker: God
decisions.reason: Elihu calls God his Maker (35:10; 36:3), as Eliphaz did (4:17). The one who made him will hold him to account for what he says.

decisions.choice: God who made me would soon put an end to me (Readable)
alternatives: my Maker would carry me away
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says plainly what "carry me away" means (m2).
